item.title: Same Market, Different Result: Why Owning More Stocks Drove the Wealth Gap
item.description: Federal Reserve 2026 Q2 data show how unequal equity ownership amplified dollar wealth gains, with important pension and classification limits.

item.title: The Top Rung Moved: What the Fed Says About the 0.1% and Where You Stand
item.description: Federal Reserve DFA data show how the top 0.1 percent pulled away from other affluent households through 2026 Q2, and what a percentile can tell you.

item.title: When to Adjust Tax Withholding Instead of Waiting for a Refund
item.description: Use the IRS Tax Withholding Estimator after an income or household change instead of treating a refund as a year-round savings plan.

item.title: Medicare Drug Bills: What the Monthly Payment Plan Changes
item.description: The Medicare Prescription Payment Plan can spread Part D out-of-pocket drug costs into capped monthly payments. It does not lower the total cost of covered prescriptions.

item.title: The 2026 HSA Limit and the Deductible Test
item.description: The 2026 HSA contribution limits are $4,400 self-only and $8,750 family. Check whether your plan meets the deductible and out-of-pocket rules before planning contributions.

item.title: A Credit Freeze Is Free: When to Use One and How to Lift It
item.description: A credit freeze is free, does not affect credit scores, and can block new-credit applications. Learn when to freeze, when to lift, and why all three bureaus matter.

item.title: Is Your Joint Bank Account Fully Insured?
item.description: FDIC joint-account coverage is generally up to $250,000 per co-owner across all qualifying joint accounts at one insured bank. Check ownership, bank, and account category before relying on the limit.

item.title: The 2026 Retirement Catch-Up Window at Ages 60 to 63
item.description: For 2026, eligible workplace-plan participants who turn 60 through 63 can use a higher catch-up limit. Check plan participation, compensation, and the Roth rule before changing payroll elections.

item.title: Emergency Funds Need a Cash-Flow Test, Not a Rule of Thumb
item.description: An emergency reserve works when cash is available before bills fall due. A cash-flow test exposes the gap that a generic months-of-expenses rule can miss.

item.title: Job Loss Hurts More When Benefits Are Not Portable
item.description: A job loss changes more than wages. Health coverage, retirement contributions and insurance can reprice the household balance sheet at once.

item.title: Disability Insurance Leaves Many Paychecks Unprotected
item.description: BLS reported that 44 percent of private-industry workers had access to short-term disability insurance and 37 percent to long-term coverage in March 2025.

item.title: How Insurance Deductibles Become a Household Balance-Sheet Shock
item.description: A health deductible is a dated cash demand. A simple liquidity test shows whether a household can absorb it without expensive financing.

item.title: America Is 2nd by Average Wealth, 15th by Median Wealth
item.description: UBS

item.title: Home Equity Is Not Emergency Liquidity
item.description: Federal Reserve and CFPB sources point to the same conclusion: home equity is real wealth, but it is not emergency liquidity on the timetable most households imagine.

item.title: Sequence Risk Before Retirement: The Fragility Nobody Prices Early Enough
item.description: Why sequence risk starts before retirement begins, why the danger is really a shrinking margin problem, and why households usually notice it only when the flexibility window is already narrower.

item.title: The Liquidity Illusion
item.description: Why household net worth, borrowing access, and practical cash resilience diverge once real conversion haircuts, deadlines, and refinancing dependence are measured directly.

item.title: The Property Tax Drag
item.description: A WealthMeter analysis of why property tax is not a side expense but a recurring carry cost that changes affordability, retirement durability, and the real value of home equity.

item.title: The Global Housing Divergence
item.description: A WealthMeter analysis of why housing markets no longer move as one trade, and how rates, supply, demographics, and policy create widening country-by-country and city-by-city divergence.

item.title: The Yield Trap in a High-Rate World
item.description: A WealthMeter analysis of why headline yield can rise while real household resilience falls, and how investors misprice duration, credit, tax, and liquidity risk when income becomes the only target.

item.title: The Freelance Freedom Tradeoff
item.description: A WealthMeter analysis of why freelance work can expand autonomy while weakening insurance, retirement automation, income stability, and the surplus needed for durable wealth building.

item.title: The Promotion Paradox
item.description: A WealthMeter analysis of why career promotions often increase status and gross income while weakening net surplus, mobility, and long-run wealth conversion.

item.title: The Debt Illusion Cycle
item.description: A WealthMeter analysis of why debt feels like wealth during expansion, how fixed obligations compound fragility, and where productive leverage differs from household self-deception.

item.title: The Windfall Misallocation Problem
item.description: A WealthMeter analysis of why inheritances, equity payouts, business exits, and other windfalls are often allocated badly because recipients confuse one-time liquidity with durable balance-sheet strength.

item.title: The Risk Tolerance Illusion
item.description: A WealthMeter analysis of why stated risk tolerance usually measures mood and recent market experience more than true balance-sheet capacity, and what a decision-grade risk framework looks like instead.

item.title: The Urban Premium Collapse
item.description: A WealthMeter analysis of why major-city income advantages no longer convert into the same after-housing, after-tax, after-time wealth premium they once did.

item.title: The Opportunity Cost of Cash
item.description: A WealthMeter analysis of when holding cash is prudent, when it becomes expensive, and how to judge the real opportunity cost by comparing liquidity value, inflation drag, and available after-tax return elsewhere.

item.title: The Venture Capital Power Law Reality
item.description: A WealthMeter analysis of why venture capital outcomes follow a power law, why that concentrates return into a tiny slice of funds and deals, and what that means for household allocation discipline.

item.title: The Productivity-Income Disconnect
item.description: A 2026 WealthMeter analysis of why productivity gains do not translate cleanly into household income, and why workers should treat that gap as a planning constraint rather than an abstract macro debate.
